subject: Term revision & true-up — performance & ROI synopsis
messages:
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
From: Elena Morales <elena@orchidtech.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Thomas Lee <thomas.lee@orchidtech.ai>; OrchidTech Finance <finance@orchidtech.ai>
Subject: Q2 usage + term check-in

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks again for the renewal reminder. Attached is our Q2 usage export and a short note on why we spiked in late May (bot testing ramp + a new personalization experiment). We’re evaluating whether to: (A) extend the current term with a small uplift, (B) true-up now and reforecast monthly, or (C) move to a higher reserved tier for steady throughput.

Key numbers in the CSV: peak token day 5.2M, avg monthly tokens 78M, embedding calls up 3x. We also saw a ~7% increase in latency-sensitive calls after the new model rollout last month.

We’d like a quick health read from your side: is the model variant we’re on optimal for cost+latency tradeoffs? And what would a 25% committed uplift look like on pricing and SLA?

Attachments: 20270610-orchid-usage-report.csv (CSV, 48 KB)

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Product
OrchidTech
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@orchidtech.ai>
Cc: Thomas Lee <thomas.lee@orchidtech.ai>
Subject: Re: Q2 usage + term check-in

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the export and the context — this is helpful. I copied in our renewal and ops leads so we can get you a concise recommendation. Quick summary from us:
- The latency jump you saw aligns with the model variant and sequence-lengths increasing after the personalization rollout. We can repro locally and have a few levers: quantized variant for embeddings, prefix caching for repeated prompts, and a slightly higher batch concurrency for steady throughput.
- Pricing: a 25% committed uplift would drop token unit cost ~11% with a small monthly credit for forecasted burst.
- SLA change: to keep p95 latency under 300ms for your traffic pattern we recommend a modest dedicated pool (1x T4-equivalent) during business hours plus on-demand burst.

I’ll schedule a short call for Monday to walk through the deck and a proposed two-option term amendment (true-up vs. uplift + dedicated corridor).

Attached: redwood-performance-deck-v2.pdf (PDF, 1.4 MB) — contains throughput/latency projections and cost scenarios.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 08:17:00 -07:00
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Subject: Fwd: Q2 usage + term check-in — internal notes

Kimberly — forwarding Elena’s export and my quick read:

On the numbers: the 78M avg/month is higher than their commit baseline (64M), but the spike days look driven by a test flag (we can ask them for the test window). If we propose a 25% uplift the committed tokens would reach ~80M/month which maps nicely to their current and projected run-rate; that reduces overage risk.

Ops recommendations (short):
- Apply prefix/KV caching for the personalization flows — should cut token billing for repeated prefixes by ~10–14%.
- Offer a short-term burst credit (one-time) to cover the May spike and show good faith on migration pains.
- Create a canary change: move 30% of traffic to quantized embeddings variant for 2 weeks to validate quality and delta in token cost.

I’ll draft two term options: (1) 12-month extension + 25% uplift with a one-time $5k burst credit, (2) 6-month true-up and revisit with usage floor + optional dedicated hours.

-Rachel
Senior Customer Success Manager
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@orchidtech.ai>
Cc: Thomas Lee <thomas.lee@orchidtech.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Subject: RE: Q2 usage + term check-in — proposal and next steps

Hi Elena / Thomas —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Based on our ops team readout, attached is the concise two-option proposal we discussed on the call this morning. TL;DR:

Option A — 12-month extension + 25% committed uplift
- Committed tokens: ~80M/month
- Unit price: -11% vs current
- One-time burst credit: $5,000 (applied to May spike)
- SLA: p95 latency target 300ms with dedicated corridor 9am–6pm PT

Option B — 6-month true-up + usage floor
- True-up for May/June usage; commit to a 70% of current run-rate as a floor
- No long-term price improvement, faster approval path
- Include a 2-week quantized embedding trial to validate cost savings

Next steps: please confirm preferred option and I’ll share a redline-ready amendment for your legal team. If helpful, Vivek and Karthik are available Thursday for a brief ops/arch sync.

Attachments: signed-MAP-draft.docx (DOCX, 18 KB)

Thanks,
Kimberly
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 16:37:00 -07:00
From: Elena Morales <elena@orchidtech.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Thomas Lee <thomas.lee@orchidtech.ai>, OrchidTech Finance <finance@orchidtech.ai>
Subject: Re: RE: Q2 usage + term check-in — proposal and next steps

Thanks Kimberly — helpful summary. Quick answers: we prefer Option A (12-month + 25% uplift) to avoid another review in 6 months. The team wants the one-time $5k burst credit in writing and the SLA clarified for business hours only. Finance wants the amendment redline today so they can sign by Friday.

Action items for you:
- Send the redline-ready amendment to finance@orchidtech.ai and cc me
- Confirm scheduled call with Vivek/Karthik on Thursday at 10:00am PT

I'll follow up with a short note about the May test window (should help explain the spike).

Best,
Elena
